QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_14

question.text: Under SEBI's performance benchmarking guidelines, performance reporting and benchmarking of the AIF Scheme must be done on which basis?

answer.text: Post-tax NAV of the Scheme at the investor level.
Pre-tax Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Scheme.
Gross Asset Value (before management fees but after tax).
Distributable Cash Flow only, excluding unrealised holdings.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 7.3 Section A (g): 'The performance reporting and benchmarking shall be carried out on pre-tax Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Scheme.' This gives a fund-level comparable basis; taxes depend on investor's residency/status and would break comparability. The Trap: Post-tax (A) introduces LP-specific tax. GAV (C) doesn't deduct fund expenses. Cash-flow-only (D) ignores residual value — both skew the benchmark. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same guideline verbatim. XXI-B PMS reports pre-performance-fee, post-expense NAV under Reg 22. Similar principle — pre-tax at the reporting vehicle.
